frontmatter.title: Golden Eagle Energy — a marginal mine priced as an option on the benchmark
frontmatter.summary: The nine-month 2026 filing is a real earnings upgrade and it fixes the 2026 cost base: stripping, capitalised stripping and haulage. Held through the licence, that cost base leaves the mine cash-negative in every forecast year, so the primary DCF finds no positive year and carries almost no value. SELL holds at Rp1,169: the shares sit at 11.2 times fundamental value.
thesis: We stay at SELL with a target of Rp1,169 against a price of Rp2,490, a total return of -52.1%.

The variant view is grade and logistics, not price direction: Triaryani's coal is a ~4,100 kcal/kg GAR product whose realised price runs at roughly a third of the Newcastle marker, and the road haul to the Lalan terminal is the largest cost line [S3] [S2].

The 2026 LK is the cost base, not an anomaly: nine-month overburden of US$28.3m plus US$19.1m of capitalised stripping is about fourteen bcm per tonne of total removal, and we hold it through FY2031E because no forward BCM schedule exists [S16].

On that basis the mine covers its cash cost only in the 2026 spike year; EBITDA is thin from FY2027E and negative from FY2028E, FCFF is negative in every forecast year, so the primary DCF carries no positive year and the value is carried by the cross-checks.
The price is a regime price: 11.2 times fundamental value, a log premium of 2.4, which the konglo lens closes only partially — hence Rp1,169 against a fundamental of Rp205.

blocks.text: **Results note, 8 November 2026 — what the nine-month print changes.** Nine-month revenue was US$147.4m, cost of sales US$125.5m and profit to owners US$14.1m [S16 p.6], with the third quarter alone larger than the whole first half [F17] [F39]. We rebuild FY2026E to 4.4 Mt, revenue of US$224.2m and profit to owners of US$18.3m, above the company's own US$12.7m plan [S2 p.96]. The overburden charge did not revert after the first half: nine months carried US$28.3m against US$8.2m for the whole of FY2025 [F55] [F11]. The LK also capitalised US$19.1m of stripping in the same nine months [F71] [S16 p.8] — about a further sixteen million bcm at the last audited cost per cubic metre — so total removal was about fourteen bcm per tonne on the nine-month tonnage, well above the historical reversion the previous edition carried. No RKAB, mine plan or public expose in the archive gives a forward BCM schedule [S2 p.20, p.81; S6], so the source-based choice is to hold the 2026 actual through the licence (strip review). The capitalised stripping stays in capex at the 2026 rate, so the model carries total removal without double counting it (capex review).

Three other changes follow from the same filing. Royalty is set at the latest effective rate the LK shows being paid, 8.2% [F57, F47], not FY2025's lower rate. Volume holds 4.4 Mt in every forecast year, the demonstrated run-rate; the company's 5.5 Mt plan is carried in the bull case with its costs, because management attributes the 2026 shortfall to the RKAB being issued late rather than to capacity [S6 p.10] (volume review). And the domestic share is set to the disclosed 25.0% local mix [S6 p.11]; the US$70.0/t cap does not bind at our realised price (domestic-cap review).

The consequence is that the base case is not a thin-margin mine but a marginal one. FY2026E earns EBITDA of US$28.7m at a benchmark near spot, but capex of US$43.7m on the annualised cash rate takes FCFF to US$-9.1m; from FY2027E EBITDA falls to US$1.6m and turns negative, with FCFF of US$-42.3m because the deck's forward price sits below the held cash cost [d.coal.newc]. No forecast year generates positive FCFF, so the primary DCF's cumulative-value rule finds no year to run. The blended fundamental value is Rp205, and the target is Rp1,169, a total return of -52.1%. **SELL** is unchanged.

We are not bearish by default. The bull case is explicit: the benchmark holds above the deck, the RKAB lifts to the company's own plan, and overburden reverts to the last disclosed full-year ratio [F10, F4]. That case is worth Rp360 and is in the scenario table. The licence extension and the associate's restart are separate, unbooked optionality.

Golden Eagle Energy began as an entertainment company and moved into coal mining this century. It is
controlled by a Singapore-listed coal group and its shares carry a very small free float, so the tape
is thin and prone to large moves on modest flow. Sub-bituminous Indonesian coal of this rank is sold
mainly to power stations, so demand tracks electricity generation rather than the steel cycle.

Golden Eagle Energy is a coal-mining holding company whose product reaches the market through PT Triaryani, a wholly-owned subsidiary holding an IUP Operasi Produksi in Musi Rawas Utara, South Sumatra [S2]. A second mine, PT Internasional Prima Coal, is a forty-nine per cent associate through PT Mega Raya Kusuma and is equity-accounted, so the income statement carries only Triaryani's revenue [S2] [S6]. The associate is a real mine that is switched off: it produced 0.7 Mt and sold 0.7 Mt in the last audited year and paid the group US$2.1m of dividends [S2] [S3], and it produced nothing in 2026 after its own permit lapsed [S6]. We mark it to its share of its own net assets, not to the carrying premium.

Triaryani's coal carries about 4,100 kcal/kg GAR with low sulphur and low ash [S2] [S6]. The group reports one segment, coal mining, and one geography [S3]. Strategically it is a capacity builder: raise output inside the annual work plan while respecting the haul-road constraint [S2]. The haulage route is the binding constraint — road to the Lalan river terminal, then barge — and the company has invested in road, jetty and barge infrastructure rather than buying tonnes [S2]. On competitive position it is a challenger: one concession, no metallurgical coal, no downstream smelter, and a public float in the low double digits [S2] [S0].

Indonesian thermal coal is a mature, policy-shaped export industry. National production fell in the last completed year and the government's high-calorie reference price fell by roughly a fifth [S2]. Domestic consumption takes a large slice through the domestic market obligation, with the balance exported [S2]. For a producer this size the binding constraints are the annual work plan and budget (RKAB), which caps tonnage, and the dollar reference prices set twice a month [S2] [S6].

The coal deck is the driver we underwrite [S2]. Its reviewed Newcastle path starts at US$137/t for the current year, steps down to US$118/t and settles at a long-run US$105/t, with spot at US$150/t flagged as a war-premium carry rather than a level the deck expects to persist [d.coal.newc]. The domestic cap sits at US$70.0/t and the low-rank markers show how steeply value falls with rank US$66.1/t [d.coal.dmo_cap, d.coal.hba_ii].

That grade ladder is our whole competitive read. A top-rank producer realises close to the seaborne benchmark; a producer at Triaryani's rank realises a fraction of it, then hands a further slice to the road haul, barge, jetty and transshipment before the coal reaches a vessel [S3]. The calibrated ratio is 0.37 of Newcastle, which at spot prices Triaryani between the deck's mid- and low-calorie markers — the right place for a ~4,100 kcal/kg GAR product [d.coal.hba_ii].

Buyer concentration is the practical constraint: 69.0% of nine-month sales went to related parties, GCI for exports and MBJT for local deliveries [F58] [S3 note 34]. Related-party gravity runs through the cost side too: the haul road and jetty are provided by PT Marga Bara Jaya, an affiliate of the controlling group, and the marketing fee the same group charges is US$1.8m [S3 note 17, note 29, note 34]. The filing does not name the haulage counterparty, so the exposure cannot be sized to the dollar from the notes. Regulation is the swing force: royalties, the domestic obligation, export proceeds retention and the frequency of RKAB resets move a marginal tonne more than a first-quartile one [S2] [S6].

The last audited year was growth with almost no margin: revenue US$103.6m, cost of sales US$95.2m, gross profit US$8.4m and EBITDA US$9.7m [S3]. The cost-of-sales note is the most revealing page: haulage at US$48.0m is the largest line, then barging, overburden, jetty and loading, then depreciation, then royalty [S3 note 28]. This is a logistics business with a mine attached.

FY2026E is the nine-month actual carried into the fourth quarter: volume 4.4 Mt, realised US$51.0 a tonne at the calibrated ratio, revenue of US$224.2m, EBITDA US$28.7m, profit to owners US$18.3m and FCFF US$-9.1m [S16]. Against the forecast, the nine-month revenue is already about two-thirds of the full year and profit about four-fifths, so the year is ahead of the pro-rata run-rate, not of the full-year forecast (results review).

Every forecast year after the current one carries the same unit economics: other cash cost US$28.3 a tonne, overburden at 8.5 bcm/t times US$1.1 a cubic metre, royalty 8.2%, and capex of US$9.9 a tonne — the 2026 cash rate, which includes the capitalised stripping and the pre-strip for the next pit [F55] [F71] [S16 p.8]. The result is the shape in the table below: EBITDA of US$1.6m in FY2027E, negative from FY2028E, and FCFF of US$-42.3m, US$-49.7m and US$-52.8m as the deck's forward price falls below the held cash cost. The mine is therefore a cash consumer at the forward curve, funded by its 2026 spike year, the shareholder loan and the bank facility. If the strip does revert, the bull case is the value (horizon review).

Depreciation is restated from the LK, not taken from the data pack: the nine-month charge in cost of sales is US$1.6m against the pack's direct-method cash-flow artefact, and the FY2025 and FY2024 charges are US$5.4m and US$10.5m [S16 note 28, S3 note 28, F54, F7, F8]. The forecast carries the last full-year rate except in FY2026E, which carries the nine-month annualised charge; the step is flagged because the LK does not explain it. Tax is the rate the latest filing shows, US$4.5m on US$18.6m of pre-tax profit [F50, F51].

Working capital is where the quality question sits (working-capital review). Related-party trade receivables rose from US$1.8m at FY2025 to US$20.7m at September [F80] [F66] [S16 p.4] — far faster than revenue, which is the divergence flag in the house screen. The customer-advance contract liability rose from US$18.7m to US$27.3m over the same period [S16 p.5, note 34], and that build is most of the gap between operating cash flow of US$23.2m and profit of US$14.1m. Read without the advance, cash conversion is close to profit rather than ahead of it. The receivables are nearly all related-party (GCI and MBJT), which makes the collection risk a related-party question, not a third-party credit question [S16 note 6, note 34].

The balance sheet is levered to the controlling shareholder and, from this year, to a bank: a short-term facility of US$20.8m secured on US$21.0m of restricted export-proceeds cash, a non-current shareholder loan of US$17.4m, and US$13.2m of unrestricted cash [S16 p.4-5]. Liquidity is adequate but not comfortable, and the export-proceeds retention keeps a large part of the cash out of reach until the facility is settled [S16 p.6, F53, F60]. Capital allocation is the other flag: the company issued 275 m shares in a non-preemptive placement for IDR220.0bn, and paid US$41.3m cash for an intermediate holding company whose disclosed assets are a fraction of the price [S2] [S3]. Both are disclosed and approved, but both dilute public holders.

Earnings quality. The accruals test passes only because of the customer advances: nine-month operating cash flow exceeds profit, but most of the excess is the related-party contract liability [F53, F52, F67]. The capitalised stripping and exploration are legitimate in this industry and disclosed, so we classify them as optics-class [S3] [S16 p.5]; the receivables divergence is the one item we would call structural, and it is now in the bear case. The associate is carried at US$24.3m against a forty-nine per cent share of its net assets of US$28.7m, so impairment, not write-up, is the direction of risk [S4] [S16 p.43], and we book the mark-down in the bridge.

The method set is the house coal card: a life-of-asset DCF at through-cycle prices as the primary method, with an EV/EBITDA cross-check and a dividend-capacity cross-check. A cyclical producer is never valued on spot earnings at the top of a cycle.

The cost of capital is built from the macro deck — a dollar risk-free rate, a mature-market equity risk premium, an Indonesia country premium, an unlevered beta and a small debt weight — giving a WACC of 10.2% and a cost of equity of 10.6%
[d.macro].
The primary DCF discounts FCFF over the licensed window with no terminal value

. The permit runs to 7 September 2031 [F68] [S16 note 1d], six years against a 314 Mt reserve [S2 p.82]. On the held 2026 cost base FCFF is negative in every forecast year, so the engine's cumulative-value rule finds no positive year: dcf_life's life_end is "none (no positive value)", its enterprise value is US$0.0m, and the discounted line is worth Rp52 — the bridge's investments and net debt, not a cash-flow value [S16]. We do not extend the horizon to rescue a value (tail review). The reserve tail beyond expiry is worth zero for two independent reasons: no Triaryani extension application is on record under PP 96/2021 Article 59 [S13], and on the held strip FCFF is negative in every in-licence forecast year (FY2026E–FY2031E), so a post-2031 extension would subtract rather than add. The licence, not the reserve, is the constraint. The extension pays only in the bull price regime, where it is the largest single upside we can name; it is not booked (licence review).
The equity bridge subtracts net debt and minorities and adds back the non-current investments where the associate sits

. The associate mark-down is booked at its share of the associate's own net assets rather than at the carrying premium; the restart is an unbooked option capped at that carrying value. Net debt corrects one data artefact: the bank facility is matched by a slightly larger restricted export-proceeds deposit that cannot be withdrawn until the facility is settled [S16 p.4-5] [F60] [F61], so deducting the loan without the deposit would overstate net debt.

The cross-checks disagree with the primary, and that is the most important disclosure here. The EV/EBITDA leg runs at 5.3 times the restated FY2025A EBITDA, giving Rp322 (EBITDA-leg review). It uses the last audited year because the pack's LTM block is empty; the nine-month trailing figure would make it higher still, so the earlier claim that it lowers the blend is withdrawn. The dividend-capacity leg gives Rp349, 571.9% above the DCF, because it capitalises the modelled twelve-month dividend at the engine's 6.9% peer-median yield (yield review); it is a peak-cycle capacity anchor on a windfall year, not a forecast, and the later years carry no dividend. With the DCF at Rp52 the blend is Rp157, and the twelve-month fundamental is Rp205. Three-fifths of that blend is a DCF the held cost base has reduced to effectively zero; if the strip reverts, the DCF recovers and the blend rises — that is the bull.

What the price implies matters most. To justify today's price on our own DCF the seaborne benchmark would have to run at 2.5 times the deck's forward path, an implied Newcastle of US$297/t against US$118/t [d.coal.newc]. The shares trade on 25.9x of our forecast earnings. Sensitivity to the benchmark and to the rupiah is wide
; the asymmetry runs against the long side, because the mine's margin is highest in the year the deck treats as a spike.

The konglo lens is the final step. The business valuation gives a fundamental twelve-month value of Rp205; the market does not trade there. At Rp2,490 the shares sit at 11.2 times the engine's pre-lens value of Rp222, a log premium of 2.4. Target = fundamental x (price / value) raised to one minus c, where c is the share of the log gap closed: 0.4 in the base regime, raised by the HSC listing and the dated free-float step together (0.1) [S7] [S8]. The regime outcomes are Rp332 (c 0.8), Rp874 and Rp2,596, blended into the target of Rp1,169.

The clearest way to lose money on the long side is to be right about coal and wrong about this company. The realised price is a fraction of the benchmark, so a strong benchmark lifts a small absolute margin; the haul, barge and jetty charges are largely fixed per tonne, so a volume shortfall spreads them over fewer tonnes; and the quota is set by the government. Regulatory risk is the highest-impact item — royalties, the domestic obligation, export-proceeds retention and quota administration bite hardest on the marginal producer. Macro risk is second: the deck flags spot as a war-premium carry, and a normalisation is a direct hit. Currency risk is modest and runs the other way, because the company earns and reports in dollars. Operational risk centres on the single haul road and the single river terminal. Governance risk is specific: related-party concentration, a controller above two-thirds of the register, a float of 11.5% and a tape thin enough that the exchange suspended it for cooling down [S5] [S6]. The HSC exclusion from the IHSG calculation and the free-float deadline can each move the price more than a quarter's earnings [S8] [S14]. Liquidity risk is minimal.

The business scenarios now carry the model's largest uncertainty (strip-shock review). Bear: the expensed stripping line climbs from 8.5 to the LK's whole ~fourteen bcm/t total-removal read while the capitalised pre-strip continues on top, so total removal is ~nineteen bcm/t — roughly a third above the base's ~fourteen — for the whole licence; the benchmark mean-reverts faster than the deck, the RKAB leaves volume light, the related-party receivable does not turn and working capital absorbs five per cent of revenue; the value is Rp145. Base: the deck path is right, the 2026 cost base holds at ~fourteen bcm/t of total removal, volume is the demonstrated run-rate and no year earns positive FCFF; the value is Rp157, against a price of Rp2,490. Bull: the benchmark holds above the deck, the RKAB lifts to the company's plan, volume reaches 5.5 Mt and the expensed overburden reverts to the disclosed FY2025 ratio, with the capitalised pre-strip still on top (~eight bcm/t total); the value is Rp360. The bear and bull bounds on the expensed line are the two sourced ends — the LK's total-removal read applied to that line and the FY2025 disclosed ratio — not a symmetric invention, and we justify the asymmetry in the assumptions record [F10, F4, F71]. The licence extension and the associate restart are excluded from all three DCFs.

Signposts that would change our view: an RKAB quota materially above the demonstrated run-rate; a reversion of the expensed strip ratio toward the historical range that persists; a renewal of the licence past September 2031 together with a benchmark that keeps the realised price above the sustaining-cost line; a restart date for the associate; and any change in the related-party share of revenue or the receivable balance.

The controlling shareholder is PT Geo Energy Investama, a subsidiary of SGX-listed Geo Energy Resources Limited, which became controller in 2023; the second holder is PT Golden Prima Energy, and public shareholders hold 11.6% [S2 p.45-47]. The exchange placed SMMT on its high-shareholding-concentration list on 22 October 2026 [S7], the IHSG exclusion is effective from 2 November 2026 [S14], and the registry's free float of 11.5% is below the new floor, with a first step to 12.5% by 31 March 2027 [S8]. We checked the ownership and pledge disclosures and found no filed pledge over the controlling stake — "none disclosed", not "none exists" [S2 p.153].

Related-party gravity is the central governance fact. 69.0% of nine-month sales went to GCI and MBJT, both affiliates; the marketing fee is paid to the same group; and the group's haul and jetty logistics run through PT Marga Bara Jaya [S3 note 17, note 29, note 34]. The borrowings are a related-party shareholder loan and a bank facility secured on restricted cash [S16 p.4-5]. This is the modal Indonesian value-destruction channel; it is disclosed, but the realised price we calibrate to is itself a related-party price — a limitation on our evidence we state plainly. No price is disclosed in the SPA, so we do not claim it sits above or below market [S3 note 27/34].

Two structure flags: the non-preemptive placement and the cash acquisition of an intermediate holding company noted in the financial section [S2] [S3]. The counterparty is not among the related parties the notes list, so we do not call it a related-party deal, but the price over acquired book, funded partly by a placement struck well below today's price, is the per-share-value-leak pattern we screen for. The audit is unqualified, in dollars, with no going-concern paragraph and no special-notation status [S2] [S3]. No dividend was paid in the last two audited years against a stated payout band [S2 p.101]. ESG exposures are the energy transition, mine rehabilitation, acid mine drainage and closure provisioning, all disclosed [S2] [S3].

The dated catalysts are the RKAB decision, the full-year audit, and the regime events. The 2027 quota sets the volume ceiling under which the whole plan operates, and the audit tests whether the nine-month cost base — stripping, capitalised stripping and haulage — is the year's run-rate [S16] [S3] [S6]. The regime events are independent of the coal price: the free-float step to 12.5% by 31 March 2027, the quarterly HSC reviews after the IHSG exclusion, the MSCI consultation decision by 30 June 2027, and any group corporate action that delivers the float [S8] [S9]. Between updates we watch a short list of KPIs: the expensed strip ratio and the capitalised-stripping additions separately, because that split distinguishes a development push from a structural cost; the realised price per tonne against the low-calorie markers; the RKAB quota and any revision; the related-party share of revenue and the related-party receivable balance; haulage cost per tonne; and the debt structure, now a bank facility larger than the shareholder loan with the export-proceeds cash pledged against it [S16 p.4-5, F60, F61, F62].

valuation.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

bear.narrative: The structural-overburden case, carried in the model and not only in the words (review C2, QC Q5): the 2026 actual cost base does not hold - the EXPENSED stripping line climbs from 8.5 to the LK's whole ~14 bcm/t total-removal read while the capitalised pre-strip continues on top, so total removal is ~19 bcm/t, about 35% above the base's ~14, for the whole licensed life and the cash margin the 2.85 bcm/t history implied never returns. Newcastle mean-reverts faster than the deck as Chinese output restarts and Indonesian supply returns; the RKAB quota leaves Triaryani volume 5% light; and the related-party receivable does not turn, raising working capital by 5% of revenue. Free cash flow is negative, the shareholder and bank loans are not repaid, the dividend stays at zero, and the associate carrying value is written down. We do NOT claim the related-party price sits above an arm's-length level: no price is disclosed in the SPA [S3 note 27/34].

bull.narrative: The war-premium bid holds and the Indonesian supply-discipline bid keeps Newcastle above the deck path, while the RKAB is lifted to the company's own 5.5 Mt plan [F14] and Triaryani's logistics allow it. Overburden reverts to the last disclosed full-year ratio of 2.85 bcm/t [F10, F4] - the sourced low bound - and working capital releases 5% of revenue as the related-party receivable turns. EBITDA and dividend capacity step up ahead of the deck. The mirror of the bear is deliberate at both bounds: 2.85 is the FY2025 disclosed expensed ratio and the bear's 14 is the LK's total-removal read applied to that same expensed line, neither is a symmetric invention, and the extension tail and the associate restart remain unbooked options.

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: Consolidated (PT Triaryani) sales tonnes, the base the consolidated P&L is built on. FY2026E is rebuilt from the HARD nine-month print: nine-month sales revenue was US$147.44m [F47] at the calibrated 0.372 realisation against the deck's nine-month Newcastle average, giving about 2.95 Mt sold; Q4 at a slightly lower run-rate (monsoon haul-road risk) gives 4.4 Mt for the year. FY2027E-FY2031E hold 4.4 Mt flat: the run-rate the group has now demonstrated. We do not carry the company's 5.5 Mt 2026 plan [F14, S2 p.96] in the base for a sourced reason: management itself attributes the 2026 output shortfall to the RKAB work-plan quota being issued only at end-March [S6 p.10], so the quota - not haul capacity alone - sets tonnage, and no 2027 RKAB is on record in the archive. The plan volume is carried in the BULL case at the same costs (volume x1.25 = 5.5 Mt, [F14]), which is the branch the most-likely card requires. The associate IPC (49%) produces nothing in 2026 [S6 p.10] and is valued through its carrying value, not through consolidated volume.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the last actual, not a forecast year: FY2025A consolidated ASP US$40.33/t (revenue US$103.62m over PT Triaryani sales 2.569 Mt [S2 p.172, S3]) divided by the FY2025A Newcastle 6,000 NAR average US$108.4/t [d.coal.newc] = 0.372. The ratio absorbs Triaryani's 4,000-4,200 kcal/kg GAR grade and its FOB/road-haul delivery point. It is corroborated, not contradicted, by the H1-2026 HARD print: ASP US$48.11/t (US$61.59m / 1.28 Mt [S4 p.6, S6 p.11]) over the H1 Newcastle average of US$128.85/t (Q1 122.3, Q2 135.4 [d.coal.newc]) = 0.373, so the FY2026E ASP of US$50.96 (0.372 x the deck's FY2026E 137.0) is the same realisation, not a better-than-plan margin (review C1). The plan's US$45.49/t implied price is below the H1 print and is rejected with its volume. Held flat: the benchmark deck carries the price path. Benchmark choice (review C12): we key on d.coal.newc because it is the industry config's price_driver for the whole COAL peer set, it carries a 20-year reviewed history, and the low-rank ICI markers (deck ici4/ici3) are not reviewable in the deck. The ratio is calibrated on the actual, so the rank discount is inside it, not assumed. Cross-check against the HBA/ICI ladder for this rank: at spot Newcastle (d.coal.newc.spot US$150.3/t) the 0.372 ratio prices Triaryani at ~US$56/t, which sits between the deck's HBA II marker (US$66.1/t) and HBA III (US$45.5/t) - the right place for a ~4,100 kcal/kg GAR product - even though the company itself attributes its September re-rating to the ICI reference price rather than Newcastle [S6 p.16]. We take that as a deliberate, sourced choice on the reviewed series. The price leg therefore follows the deck's full-year path while the cost leg is anchored on the H1 print - a disclosed asymmetry, stated in §3, and symmetrical only in that the bear/bull shocks hit the same price path by mirrored amounts [d.coal.newc, S4 p.6, S6 p.11].

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: Set to the disclosed domestic mix, not to the engine default (review C9): the 20 Oct 2026 public expose states that local sales reached 25% of 2026 volume [S6 p.11], and the covered coal peers carry 0.22-0.50. The US$70/t domestic cap [d.coal.dmo_cap] does not bind at our realised price - the calibrated 0.372 ratio on the deck's FY2026E Newcastle marker prices FY2026E at about US$51/t, more than a third below the cap - so the 25% domestic share has no effect on blended revenue in any forecast year; the input is set for disclosure consistency and would only bind in a benchmark spike above US$188/t at this ratio [d.coal.dmo_cap, S6 p.11].

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne)
assumptions.basis: HELD AT THE 2026 ACTUAL THROUGH THE LICENCE (review C1). No RKAB, mine plan or public expose in the archive gives a forward BCM schedule [S2 p.20, p.81; S6], so the last actual governs every forecast year: the stripping charge expensed in cost of sales was US$28.30m for nine months [F55] which, at the FY2025 cost of US$1.15/bcm [F11], is about 24.6 Mbcm; Q4 at the Q3 rate puts the year near 37 Mbcm over 4.4 Mt, or 8.5 bcm/t. The last disclosed full-year ratio is 2.77/3.23/2.85 bcm/t for FY2023-FY2025 (7,130,388 BCM [F10] over 2,499,701 t [F4]), but the 2026 LK contradicts it, so that reversion is withdrawn from the base. The LK also capitalised US$19.14m of stripping in the same nine months [F71, S16 p.8] - a further ~16.6 Mbcm, ~41.3 Mbcm in nine months, or ~14 bcm/t of total removal on the nine-month 2.95 Mt [F47, F48, F54, F55, F57] - and that capitalised portion is carried in capex_unit at US$9.93/t (of which ~US$6.49/t is stripping), so the DCF carries the total removal and does not double count it. The bear case raises the expensed line to 14 bcm/t and keeps the capitalised ~5 on top (~19 total); the bull carries the disclosed FY2025 2.85 bcm/t expensed plus the same capitalised ~5 (~8 total).

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm
assumptions.basis: FY2025A overburden removal expense US$8,182,359 [S3 note 28] over 7,130,388 BCM removed [S2 p.20] = US$1.15/bcm; held at the last actual in real terms.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Set from the LK, not left at the template default (review C13). The term scales the mining block (strip_ratio x cost_per_bcm, i.e. the overburden charge), so fuel is taken as its share of that block: fuel US$337,850 [S3 note 28, F26] over the overburden charge US$8,182,359 [S3 note 28, F11] = 4.1%. Fuel is 0.37% of the US$90.4m total production cost, so the round-1 0.3 default overstated the group's oil exposure roughly sevenfold; a real Brent move now barely moves unit cost.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, jetty, process)
assumptions.basis: Recalibrated to the nine-month HARD print on a consistent cash-cost definition. Nine-month cost of sales US$125,540,863 less government royalty US$12,095,609 less the full cost-of-sales depreciation and amortisation line of US$1,595,105 less overburden US$28,301,968 = US$83,548,181 over nine-month sales of about 2.95 Mt [F47, F48, F54, F55, F57] = US$28.32/t. All non-cash amortisation is stripped out and is not double-charged through the D&A line. This is the road-haul/barge/jetty/transshipment block; it ran about 1% below the H1-2026 rate of US$29.97/t as hauling cost per tonne fell in Q3, and we carry the latest actual in real terms. The overburden line is NOT in this unit rate: it is modelled separately through strip_ratio x cost_per_bcm.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: The LATEST effective rate the LK shows being paid, not the FY2025 rate (review C10): nine-month 2026 government royalty US$12,095,609 on sales US$147,443,098 = 8.20% [F57, F47, S16 note 29]. FY2025 was 7.86% (US$8,148,886 on US$103,617,931) and FY2024 7.76% [S3 note 28], so the paid rate stepped up in 2026; the covered coal peers pay 8.8-14.8% (ARII 8.8%, PTBA 10.3%, ITMG 11.7%, GEMS 12.9%), so 8.20% is not a conservative assumption. Under PP 19/2025 the IUP open-pit schedule for the 4,000-4,200 kcal/kg GAR tranche is 5%/6%/9% by HBA band, which brackets rather than matches the paid rate; the rate paid governs per the house rule.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: the group reports a single coal-mining segment with no other revenue line [S3 note 35].

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: D&A per unit
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is set on the nine-month print: depreciation and amortisation charged to cost of sales was US$1,595,105 for nine months [F54], of which US$936,145 fell in Q3, so a full year at the Q3 rate is about US$2.5m, or US$0.57/t on 4.4 Mt. This is far below FY2025's US$5.43m [F7] because the mining-property amortisation run down; the LK does not explain the step, so it is flagged. FY2027E-FY2030E keep the last full-year rate of US$2.11/t as the stripping activity asset is amortised over future production. The data pack's D&A remains the direct-method cash-flow artefact and is restated from the LK [S3, S16].

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit
assumptions.basis: HELD AT THE 2026 ACTUAL RATE ON THE TONNAGE IT WAS SPENT ON, through the licence (reviews C1, C10 and QC Q1), not cut to the depreciation rate and not diluted over a volume the spend did not cover. The nine-month cash spend was additions to the stripping activity asset US$19,144,461, exploration and evaluation US$7,591,693, PP&E US$1,574,147, mining properties US$161,031 and advances US$813,544 = US$29,284,876 [F71, S16 p.8, p.10] against nine-month sales of about 2.95 Mt [F47, F48, F54, F55, F57], i.e. US$9.93/t. QC Q1 is right that the earlier US$6.66/t divided the full nine-month spend by the full-year 4.4 Mt volume and so understated capex by ~33%; on the model's 4.4 Mt that is US$43.7m a year. Two components matter: the capitalised stripping (~US$6.49/t, ~16.6 Mbcm at US$1.15/bcm) is the part of total overburden removal that the expensed strip_ratio of 8.5 does not carry, and holding it keeps the DCF on the LK's ~14 bcm/t total-removal basis; the exploration and evaluation spend is the pre-strip for the next pit. No mine plan or RKAB shows either programme ending [S2 p.99], so both are held in real terms rather than reverting to the FY2025 D&A rate, which is an unexplained depreciation proxy. Annualising the nine-month cash spend, not diluting it, is the sourced rate.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: 2025 capex was routine infrastructure, with no large expansion commitment outstanding [S2 p.94].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A, sourced to the data pack

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Set to the rate the latest LK shows being paid, per the house rule: income tax expense US$4,475,768 on profit before tax US$18,590,275 = 24.08% for nine months to September 2026 [F50, F51], against 34.07% in FY2025 [S3] and 8.3-8.6% in FY2023-FY2024. The FY2025 rate carried a deferred-tax build (deferred tax liabilities rose from US$0.67m to US$4.73m in nine months, [S16 p.5]) and is not repeated in the base. 24.1% is the forward anchor; it is above the 22% statutory rate because of non-deductible items, and it stays flat across the forecast.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The LK shows the cost: interest expense US$1,263,723 for nine months [F72], annualised at US$1.68m, on average gross debt of US$32.8m (US$27.29m at 31 Dec 2025 to US$38.24m at 30 Sep 2026) = about 5.1%. The related-party shareholder loan and the bank facility are the only borrowings [S16 p.5].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A over the data pack

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the actual step in gross debt between 31 Dec 2025 and 30 Sep 2026: gross debt rose from US$27.29m (shareholder loan) to US$38.24m (shareholder loan US$17.42m [F62] plus short-term bank loan US$20.82m [F61]), i.e. +US$10.95m, as the group funded the Q3 working-capital and capitalised-stripping build [S16 p.5]. The shareholder loan was repaid down by US$9.87m and the bank facility drawn up. No further facility is committed, so FY2027E onward is zero and the balance is held flat [S2].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A; minorities are immaterial (0.2% of equity at FY2025) [S3].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The stated dividend policy is a 15%-30% payout of net profit after tax [S2 p.101]; 25% is the policy midpoint and the most-likely forward anchor, not a cautious one (review C10). Track record is mixed but not hostile: the company paid nothing in FY2024 and FY2025 [S2 p.101], yet it paid a first interim cash dividend of Rp37/share at a 72% payout in FY2023 when cash allowed [S2 p.101], above the policy band, so it pays when it can. The FY2026E modelled year carries free cash flow of US$30.1m and builds net cash, so the 25% is fundable; the model uses it as the normalised rate rather than the zero of a capex-heavy year. At the recalibrated H1-2026 cost base the FY2026E modelled year still carries positive free cash flow, but the later years are negative at the deck's forward prices, so the 25% payout is a policy anchor, not a cash forecast. The dividend yield cross-check is a capacity anchor capitalised on the peak-cycle DPS; §4 discloses the through-cycle value and the leg carries its configured 15% weight (review C4).

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: the 2025 private placement of 275m shares is complete and no further issue is guided [S2 p.102].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: house long-run USD inflation (macro deck inflation_usd_lt 2.0%) applied to the cross-check DCF; the primary dcf_life carries no terminal value.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the last actual: FY2025 general, administrative and selling expense US$3,461,685 plus the mining final-tax charge inside the pack's opex line = US$4,102,146 on revenue US$103,617,931 = 3.96% [S3]. The three-year average (5.65%) is inflated by the thin FY2023 revenue base.

challenges.section: 3. Financial analysis and forecasts; fund record strip_ratio
challenges.challenge: strip_ratio sets FY2026E 8.5 and FY2027E-FY2030E 2.85 bcm/t, a -66% step that carries the entire DCF. The 8.5 counts only the cost-of-sales line (US$28.30m for 9M [F55]); the LK also capitalises US$19.14m of stripping in the same nine months [F71, S16 p.8], which at US$1.15/bcm [F11] is a further 16.6 Mbcm, so total removal was about 41.3 Mbcm on about 2.95 Mt = about 14 bcm/t, not 8.5. The report charges that capitalised spend in FY2026E capex but excludes it from the evidence for the 2027 rate, and admits no mine plan, RKAB or presentation gives a forward BCM schedule. Holding the 2026 rate through FY2031E removes about US$28m a year (FY2027E EBITDA 29.7 to about 2) and takes the DCF from Rp200 to near zero. This is the largest value lever in the report and the direction is optimistic.
challenges.answer: Held the 2026 actual strip of 8.5 bcm/t through FY2031E and withdrew the FY2025 reversion; the DCF now stops after FY2026E and the value is shown in 4. Valuation [S16].

challenges.section: 5. Investment risks and scenario analysis; fund record scenarios.bear
challenges.challenge: fund record strip_ratio says if the elevated rate is structural rather than developmental the bear case carries it, but the bear scenario's shocks are newc x0.8, volume x0.95 and realisation x0.9 - no strip or cost shock - and the section 5 bear narrative never mentions overburden. The claim that the bear carries the model's largest uncertainty is false, so the bear value of Rp57 is not the downside the report describes.
challenges.answer: The bear now holds total removal at the ~14 bcm/t LK read (strip shock x1.647) and adds a working-capital shock; the bear value is shown in 5. Risks [S16] [F71].

challenges.section: Investment summary; thesis bullet 4; 4. Valuation; 5. Investment risks
challenges.challenge: The summary, thesis bullet 4, section 4 and section 5 all say the realised price does not cover sustaining capital and that FCF is thin through the licensed life. The model's own lines contradict this: EBITDA US$29.7m v capex US$8.9m in FY2027E, US$19.2m v US$9.1m in FY2028E, US$15.8m v US$9.5m in FY2031E, and FCFF is positive in every year (5.9, 13.2, 7.1, 2.1, 4.9, 5.0). The claim holds only at the deck's long-run marker of US$105 (realised about US$39.1), where margin is roughly breakeven; on the modelled path the mine covers sustaining capex 1.7-3.4x.
challenges.answer: Rewrote the claim: the mine covers cash cost only in FY2026E; from FY2027E EBITDA is thin and turns negative, so the DCF runs one year [S16].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 justifies valuing the 314 Mt reserve beyond 2031 at zero by asserting the present value of the years beyond the licence is negative and that half, three-quarters and full extension are each a fraction of a negative number. The same record says the dcf_life runs every licensed year because FCFF is positive in each, and FY2031E FCFF is +US$5.03m with EBITDA US$15.8m against capex US$9.5m. A year on FY2031E economics is positive, not negative, so the arithmetic is wrong and about 92% of the reserve is zeroed on an unsupported claim. This is an unjustified conservatism and the largest upside omitted from the fundamental.
challenges.answer: The horizon stops at the licence end on 7 September 2031 [F68, S16 note 1d], and the engine's cumulative-value rule finds no positive year because FCFF is negative in every forecast year (FY2026E-FY2031E) on the held strip, so life_end is 'none (no positive value)', not a one-year run, and the DCF is effectively zero. The earlier 'post-2031 FCFF is negative' shorthand was wrong - the negative years are inside the licence (FY2027E-FY2031E) - and is corrected in 4. Valuation and the horizon.reserves justification. The reserve tail is zero because the licence ends in 2031 and no extension is on record [S13], not from a post-2031 arithmetic.

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA leg is dropped because the data pack's trailing period carries no EBITDA field, so the metric cannot be computed at all. The LTM block carries ebit US$18.65m and the LK gives D&A for FY2025 (US$5.43m [F7]), 9M26 (US$1.60m [F54]) and 9M25 (US$2.45m [F46]): LTM EBITDA about US$23.2m. The house rule is to restate data, not model around it. The stated direction is also wrong: a peer-median EV/EBITDA (AADI 2.09x, PTBA/ITMG single-digit) applied to US$23.2m sits above the DCF's Rp200, so adding the leg would raise the blend, not lower it as section 4 claims.
challenges.answer: Restored the EV/EBITDA leg at 5.3x restated FY2025A EBITDA and corrected the direction: it raises the blend rather than lowering it [S3].

challenges.section: 4. Valuation; 5. Investment risks and scenario analysis
challenges.challenge: The report names the licence extension (the largest single upside we can name, section 5) and the IPC restart as the upside, but neither is in any scenario: the bull shocks are newc x1.2, volume x1.05 and realisation x1.1, and the dcf_life horizon is FY2031E for every run, so the bull Rp1,143 also excludes the tail. Section 4 says the extension pays in the bull price regime and that is where the report says so - it is not in the bull model run.
challenges.answer: The licence extension and associate restart are now named in 4 and 5 as unbooked optionality rather than omitted from the scenarios [S13].

challenges.challenge: Volume is 4.4 Mt for FY2026E and 4.2-4.4 Mt for FY2027E-FY2030E, 20-24% below the company's own 5.5 Mt plan [F14, S2 p.96] and far below the Q3 run-rate implied by US$85.85m of quarterly revenue (about 1.67 Mt, about 6.7 Mt annualised). The stated reason not to use the plan is that its implied price is US$45.49/t - a price objection, not a volume one - and no RKAB ceiling is cited. The most-likely card says volume follows the plan or capacity unless reserves or contracts say otherwise; this is a default haircut.
challenges.answer: Volume holds the nine-month run-rate of 4.4 Mt; the 5.5 Mt plan is carried in the bull with its costs because the RKAB was late, not capacity [S6].

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality paragraph says the accruals test is not a concern and does not mention working capital, yet trade receivables rose from US$2.93m at 31 Dec 2025 to US$22.25m at 30 Sep 2026 [S16 p.4, note 6], 7.6x against revenue growth of 63%, and 93% of the balance is related-party (GCI US$12.58m, MBJT US$8.08m). The US$27.31m related-party contract liability [F67] is a large part of why 9M CFO (US$23.2m) exceeds profit (US$14.1m). Neither the receivables jump nor that dependence is in the bear case or the quality screen (EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS divergence flag at >1.5x revenue growth).
challenges.answer: Added related-party receivable and contract-liability facts, prose on the divergence, and a working-capital shock in the bear [S16 note 6].

challenges.challenge: Every covered coal peer carries a domestic capped share (AADI 0.25, ARII 0.50, BSSR 0.30, ITMG 0.22, PTBA 0.35, GEMS 0.30) and SMMT's own Q2 expose says 25% of 2026 sales are local [S6 p.11], but SMMT's inputs carry capped_share 0.0 and the model runs one realisation ratio with no DMO/HBA split. The industry config also sets cap_driver d.coal.dmo_cap and royalty_index d.coal.hba, both dropped (royalty is a flat override, justified). At the deck's prices the US$70 cap does not bind, but the input is inconsistent with peers and the disclosure, and the bull's wider-mix argument cannot be tested without the split.
challenges.answer: Domestic share set to the disclosed 25 percent local mix; the dollar cap does not bind at our realised price [S6].

challenges.challenge: Unjustified optimism, the direction that raises the target - royalty held at 7.86% although the 9M 2026 LK rate is 8.20% [F57/F47] and every covered peer runs 8.8-14.8% (ARII 8.8%, PTBA 10.3%, ITMG 11.7%, GEMS 12.9%); the strip reversion (C1); capex cut to US$2.11/t from the US$6.66/t nine-month actual; and a dividend-capacity leg at Rp359 on a 25% payout of a windfall year. Unjustified conservatism: the post-2031 reserve at zero (C4) and the IPC stake at book. The optimistic items outnumber and outweigh the conservative ones; the rating does not flip, but Rp411 is more likely too high than too low.
challenges.answer: Royalty set to the latest paid 8.20 percent; capex held at the 2026 6.66 per tonne cash rate including capitalised stripping, shown in the stack [S16 p.8] [F57].

challenges.challenge: The div-yield leg's 6.89% peer median has no citation and section 4 cites [S2], the company's own annual report, for it; a peer median cannot come from SMMT's filings. Separately, section 6 calls the GCI contract a single related-party sale though the LK's note 34 groups both GCI (US$94.8m) and MBJT (receivables US$8.08m) as related parties.
challenges.answer: The dividend leg is labelled the engine's peer-median yield on a windfall year, and MBJT is named as the local related-party buyer [S3 note 34].

challenges.challenge: The results note is 9,552 words against a house range of 500-3,500 for a results note (fund record check), and it duplicates: section 4 renders table:valuation twice, and the free-float/HSC/MSCI material appears in sections 4, 5, 6 and 7. At 2.7x the ceiling the three things that move value are buried in repeated standing material.
challenges.answer: The report is cut to the results-note length with duplicate passages removed and the evidence retained [S2].

challenges.challenge: Three fundamental values and premium ratios are stated: Rp414 and 6.12x (qc_justifications konglo.overlay), Rp411 and 6.2 times (report text and val.tp_fundamental 411.32) and Rp403.65 at 6.17x (the engine's konglo.v_fundamental that actually drives the Rp1,455 target). 2,490/411.32 = 6.05x, and the report's stated identity target = fundamental x premium kept gives Rp1,481, not Rp1,455.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now reconciles the pre-lens value, the fundamental and the target through the konglo lens arithmetic [S7] [S8].

challenges.challenge: The catalyst dated 2026-11-06 says the Q3 LK showed nine-month revenue and profit ahead of the full-year forecast; 9M revenue US$147.4m is 66% of the FY2026E US$224.2m and 9M profit US$14.1m is 75% of US$18.9m, so it is ahead of the pro-rata run-rate, not of the full-year forecast. Two of the seven catalysts (2 Nov and 6 Nov) are already past at asof 8 Nov.
challenges.answer: Catalysts are re-dated after the as-of date and the actual-versus-forecast comparison is stated in section 3 [S16].

missing_bull_case.note: The two upsides the report itself names as largest - the post-2031 licence extension (314 Mt reserve, 71 years, only 8% inside the DCF) and the IPC restart - are in no scenario: the bull shocks are newc x1.2, volume x1.05, realisation x1.1 and the dcf_life horizon is FY2031E for every run, so the bull Rp1,143 also excludes the tail (C6). Volume is also set 20-24% below the company's own 5.5 Mt plan on a price objection, not a quota (C7).

missing_bear_case.note: fund record says the bear case carries the structural-elevation strip risk, but the bear shocks contain no cost or strip component (newc x0.8, volume x0.95, realisation x0.9) and the section 5 bear narrative never mentions overburden (C2). Trade receivables rising to US$22.25m, 93% related-party, and the US$27.3m related-party customer advance behind the CFO figure are absent from the bear and from the earnings-quality screen (C8). The free-float supply channel is well quantified - credit.

assumption_realism.note: Benchmark, volume, cost/bcm, other cash cost, D&A and tax are anchored on the LK or the last actual, and the 9M reconciliation is sound. The three value drivers are not equal, though: the strip ratio reverts 8.5 to 2.85 bcm/t (-66%) on an inference the record admits is unsourced, and total 9M overburden removal is about 14 bcm/t once the US$19.1m capitalised strip is counted, not 8.5 (C1); that single line moves FY2027E EBITDA from US$29.7m to about US$2m. Volume runs below both plan and the Q3 run-rate without an RKAB source (C7).

evidence_and_citations.note: Spot-checked in S16 and confirmed - 9M revenue 147,443,098, COGS 125,540,863, overburden 28,301,968, restricted cash 21,000,000, cash 13,214,641, short-term bank loan 20,821,719, shareholder loan 17,418,602, IPC 49% share of net assets 14,067,981, 69% related-party sales, licence to 7 Sep 2031 - and the 2.93m to 22.25m receivables jump is in note 6. Gaps: the div-yield leg's 6.89% peer median is uncited and is cited to S2, the company's own annual report (C11); three different fundamental values/premium ratios appear in the record (C13); the frontmatter overstates the Q3 beat (C14). No broker, rating, target or consensus number appears anywhere - clean.

valuation_method_fit.note: Primary dcf_life on the licensed window, flat royalty at the LK effective rate, net debt/minorities/associates bridged item by item, cost of capital from the macro deck: all correct per the coal card. But the EV/EBITDA cross-check is dropped on an avoidable data gap (LTM ebit 18.65 plus LK D&A gives about 23.2m) and the stated direction is wrong (C5), and the terminal treatment is justified by an arithmetic claim the record contradicts (C4). The konglo overlay is applied correctly at c 0.3 plus 0.05 and 0.05 per the deck, and the report refuses to raise c for the 2 Nov exclusion - correct.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose says more than the model: does not cover sustaining capital and thin FCF through the licensed life are contradicted by the EBITDA-versus-capex lines in every forecast year after FY2026E (C3). The SELL itself is not heroic - the price is 6x the fundamental value and the call survives a doubled bear - but the report understates its own cash generation and overstates its cost certainty, in the same direction as the rating. Two contradictory directions (strip optimism, tail pessimism) partly offset.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Right deck variables read (d.coal.newc, d.coal.hba_ii, d.coal.dmo_cap in the text; cost currency USD; IUP licence and flat effective royalty). But capped_share is 0.0 against 0.25-0.50 for every covered coal peer and 25% local sales in the company's own Q2 expose, and the industry's cap_driver and HBA royalty index are dropped - the US$70 cap does not bind at the deck price, but the input is inconsistent and the mix shift the bull assumes cannot be tested (C9). Royalty at 7.86% is the lowest in the peer set (C10). MATERIAL on the input, not on the value.

conservatism_audit.note: Below the last actual, guidance or the LK rate: royalty 7.86% vs 9M 8.20% and peers 8.8-14.8% (C10); capex 2.11/t vs 6.66/t actual (sourced to the D&A proxy, disclosed as optimism); strip 2.85 vs 8.5 actual (the largest, C1); dividend leg on a windfall year. Above (conservative): the whole post-2031 reserve at zero (C4); IPC marked to book (-US$10.1m, defensible given the expired IUP); the volume haircut is the opposite direction. The optimism stack outweighs the conservatism and raises the fundamental, but the rating does not flip on any single item.

calibration.note: qc returns no blocking flag but the calibration gate is substantively failed: FY2025A re-priced at the FY2026E cost base gives EBITDA -6.52m against the actual +9.72m (-167%), and the justification attributes the whole gap to a real 2026 cost step that the same model then unwinds from FY2027E. A model that cannot reproduce the last actual at the cost base it uses for FY2027-31 is carrying an unresolved break, not a calibrated forecast (C1). The other BLOCK flags (drift.da_unit, drift.capex_unit, royalty.flat, horizon.reserves, extreme_call) are each answered with a source and are acceptable as written.

signoff.notes: Approved on substance; the three honesty tests the desk gives a zero-DCF name all pass. (1) The zero DCF is on its face, not hidden: s4 says the discounted line is 'worth Rp52 - the bridge's investments and net debt, not a cash-flow value', that 'three-fifths of that blend is a DCF the held cost base has reduced to effectively zero', and it calls the cross-check disagreement 'the most important disclosure here'. Nothing is labelled life-of-asset value that is not. The engine's dcf_life rule truncates at the year that maximises cumulative value: on the held 2026 cost base FCFF is negative in every forecast year (FY2026E-FY2031E), so no year adds value, life_end is 'none (no positive value)', and the DCF contributes effectively nothing. The earlier edition wrongly described a positive FY2026E year and a 'six-year' run; both are corrected here. Extending the horizon would subtract value, not add it, so the licence end and the negative arithmetic point the same way.
